instruction.text: A pizza was cut into 8 equal slices. Paula eats 6 slices. Answer the questions.

atoms.a: What fraction of the pizza did she eat?
atoms.b: She ate <mat><gap>6</gap>/8</mat> of the pizza. This fraction is equivalent to <mat><gap>3</gap>/4</mat>.

atoms.a: What is the decimal equivalent of this fraction?
She buys another pizza and eats 4 slices. What fraction of this pizza did she eat?
atoms.b: She ate <mat><gap>4</gap>/8</mat> of the pizza. This fraction is equivalent to <mat><gap>1</gap>/2</mat>.

atoms.a: What is the decimal equivalent of this fraction?
Did she eat more of the first or more of the second pizza?
atoms.b: She ate more of the ((++first second)) pizza.

instruction.text: Max is baking, but his measuring cup only has decimal markings. Answer the questions.

atoms.a: The recipe needs <mat>1/2</mat> a cup of milk. What is the decimal equivalent of <mat>1/2</mat>?
The recipe also needs <mat>3/4</mat> of a cup of flour. What is the decimal equivalent of <mat>3/4</mat>?
Does the recipe need more flour or more milk?

instruction.text: A ribbon is 1 metre long. Answer the questions.

atoms.a: Angela needs to cut <mat>1/4</mat> of the ribbon to wrap around a present. How many metres of ribbon does she need to cut?
atoms.b: She needs to cut <mat><gap>0.25</gap></mat> metres of ribbon.

atoms.a: What fraction of the ribbon is left uncut?
atoms.b: <mat><gap>3</gap>/<gap>4</gap></mat> of the ribbon is left uncut.

atoms.a: How many metres of ribbon are left?
atoms.b: There are <mat><gap>0.75</gap></mat> metres of ribbon left.
